memory_update.text: Vestis is the strongest underfollowed direct fit for hospitality facility services and linen/uniform route-density exposure; it has direct hospitality/customer-location disclosure and recurring rental economics.
ABM is an adjacent underfollowed candidate for hospitality facility-services exposure, but the purity of hotel/restaurant demand linkage needs segment and customer-end-market verification.
UniFirst remains a useful direct comparable for uniform rental and facility-service economics, but the March 2026 Cintas acquisition agreement reduces its standalone discovery value.

The node appears to be driven less by headline consumer demand and more by route density, recurring rental contracts, local processing capacity, labor availability, hygiene/compliance requirements, and retention of commercial accounts.

Need a later-layer evidence pass on market caps, analyst coverage, vertical revenue exposure, route-count data, contract retention, wage/fuel/energy/water sensitivity, and customer churn for VSTS, ABM, and UNF.

node: Hospitality facility services, linen, uniforms, cleaning, laundry, and maintenance networks
summary: Expanded the underfollowed public-company universe around hospitality and restaurant facility-service chokepoints. The best fits are route-density and recurring-service models that touch uniforms, linens, mats, towels, restroom supplies, janitorial services, engineering maintenance, and workplace hygiene. Reference leader Cintas helps define the model, while Vestis, ABM, and UniFirst represent smaller or less centrally followed exposure. UniFirst is now transaction-linked after the March 2026 Cintas acquisition agreement, so its standalone discovery value is reduced but it remains useful as an industry-comparable and evidence anchor.
